description: Show what a Blender scene looks like: a fast, low-cost preview render on a cloud GPU, back as an image in seconds. Typical requests: 'render this .blend', 'show me the scene', 'preview the turntable', 'I have no GPU', 'Blender is too slow on my laptop', 'Blenderでレンダリングして', 'GPUがない', 'ターンテーブル', '商品の360度動画'. Also use it after writing a bpy script, to see what it builds. Each preview returns a critic verdict (ok / check / fix) with fix code: apply the fixes and preview again before any final render. It also returns final_estimate (the same scene as a 1080p final) and quota_left_today; tell the user both before asking to go on. Prices come before rendering: final_offers give each next render's time and price, and a paid one needs the user's approval. A script that raises comes back as a failure with the line (nothing is rendered). When not to use: editing a scene open in the user's Blender belongs to a local Blender MCP, and a single still on a machine with its own NVIDIA GPU usually renders faster locally. This service is for CPU-only machines, animations, and scripts with no Blender installed. Limits: up to 1280x720; 1-4 frames tiled in one labeled image for the GPU time of one 720p frame. preset='product' | 'turntable' | 'animation' sets camera, light, backdrop and frames for that purpose. Other options are explained on each parameter: environment presets and 'compare', orbit (turntable), cameras (several named cameras), engine, transparent, asset_urls with 'polyhaven:<id>' CC0 assets. Give the scene as scene_script (bpy code as text), scene_url (an https link to a .blend, .py or 3D file) or scene_id; reuse the returned scene_id in render_final.

scene_script.title: Scene Script
scene_script.description: The scene as bpy Python code (text). No file and no local Blender needed; the service runs it in Blender 5.0 (5.2 with blender='5.2'). Blender 5.0 API notes: materials are node-based, so set a colour on the Principled BSDF (mat.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF'].inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (r, g, b, 1)); mat.diffuse_color only affects the viewport; do not set Material.use_nodes. Animate with obj.keyframe_insert() (action.fcurves no longer exists; set bpy.context.preferences.edit.keyframe_new_interpolation_type = 'LINEAR' first for constant speed). Build the scene, camera and frame range only; leave resolution, samples and denoising to the service. Helpers: `import jr_assets`, then jr_assets.frame_camera(margin=1.1) points the camera at every object and fits them in the frame; jr_assets.import_model('<id>'), jr_assets.material('<id>') and jr_assets.world_hdri('<id>') use Poly Haven assets passed in asset_urls.

scene_url.title: Scene Url

A .gltf or .obj also brings its .bin / .mtl / textures from the same folder.

description: Render the final frames or video of a Blender scene on cloud GPUs, after the user approved a preview: 'render the final', 'make the video', 'export the turntable MP4'. description: Check the connection and the service before rendering (read-only, no GPU time, no charge): the server URL, whether GPU workers are online, the queue length and expected wait, and this key's usage. Use it before the first render or when renders seem stuck, and to decide whether to route a render here: workers_available > 0 means a preview comes back in seconds; gated means the GPU is lent out and gate says how long the wait usually is. It runs as the connected account (OAuth or the API key in the connector). Every call is rate-limited per key; a 429 response carries retry_after_s, wait that long. diagnose.tell_user says in plain words whether the connection, the key, the free credit and the GPUs are fine and what the last failed render said; relay it when the user asks why something does not work.

description: Find free CC0 3D models, PBR textures or HDRIs on Poly Haven by words ('wooden chair', 'forest hdri') to furnish a scene without uploading files; no GPU time. For product shots of something the user has no model for: asset_search('<item>'), then render_preview(scene_script='import jr_assets; jr_assets.import_model("<id>")', asset_urls=['polyhaven:<id>'], preset='product') gives 4 studio shots on a plain backdrop (import_model removes Blender's untouched startup cube first). Each result has a spec 'polyhaven:<id>' to pass in asset_urls, its size in metres and the entry file. In the scene script: import jr_assets, then jr_assets.import_model('<id>', location=(x, y, z), scale=1.0) returns the objects, jr_assets.material('<id>') builds a material and jr_assets.apply(obj, mat) assigns it, jr_assets.world_hdri('<id>', strength=1.0) lights the world. 'polyhaven:<id>@2k' fetches 2k textures (1k by default).

This cannot be undone: sharing again makes a new page with a new URL. The job's own files are not touched (they expire on their usual schedule). Only the key that shared the job can take the page down; a job without a share page returns not_found.

description: Stop a queued or running render job of this key (a j_... job, or a b_... job split into parts, which stops every part). Effects: queued frames are dropped; frames already rendered are charged and stay downloadable until the job expires; the rest of the GPU time held for the job is returned to the key at once. It cannot be undone or resumed: to render again, call render_final again (a new job). A job that is already done, failed or canceled is returned unchanged, and a job whose frames are all rendered and is being assembled into the video cannot be stopped (nothing more is charged). Only the key that started the job can stop it; any other job_id returns not_found. Ask the user before cancelling a render they asked for.

    cameras and frame range, and render_preview(scene_id=...) to see it. Nothing is rendered or charged here. A large file
    can take a few minutes: if the reply says status 'importing', call render_import_file again with the same file after
    about 30 seconds (the download continues and is not started again). If the attachment cannot be fetched, ask the user
    to attach it again or to upload it at the /upload page.
